text:
Starting this morning, seasonal high tides up and down the coast of California are expected to drive “major to extreme” coastal flooding, with the San Francisco Bay Area currently seen as being at the highest risk of travel-related flooding delays.
The first of the year’s highest “king tides” will arrive in much of southern California, including parts of San Diego and Los Angeles, before 9am on Tuesday, and in the Bay Area between 10 and 11am, according to tidal estimates from the California Coastal Commission.
The combination of seasonal high tides and higher ocean levels from this season’s Super El Niño weather is expected to inundate low-lying areas near coasts and bays, with many experts predicting record-setting high water levels.
In San Francisco, Tuesday morning’s high tide is expected to be 2.6ft (79.2cm) above normal, according to the National Weather Service.
California’s north coast, around Humboldt bay, may see “some of the worst effects” because of the combination of high water levels with strong winds and heavy rains, which is likely to “wreak some havoc along the Highway 101 and Highway 1 corridors”, California climate scientist Daniel Swain said in a briefing on Monday.
While San Francisco will also see some rain in combination with the high tides, the Bay Area storm is expected to be lighter than previously feared. However, “we may still approach or exceed all-time record water levels even without a significant storm,” Swain said.
San Francisco’s mayor Daniel Lurie, who had been telling San Franciscans to brace for “high tides and rain that this city has never seen before” and asked residents to avoid inessential travel on Monday through Wednesday, said on Monday that the forecast had “improved”, and that the worst impacts from the high tides were predicted to peak Wednesday at 11am. He advised: “Monday and Tuesday are the best days to travel and to do your errands.” The San Francisco Chronicle published a guide to the best and worst times to be out on the roads across the region on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
Swain, the climate scientist, said there had been “severe miscommunications” in public messaging about the flood risk, and said he believed San Francisco officials had originally overhyped the geographical range of the flooding danger. “There is real risk along the immediate coast, but there’s almost no risk of inundation at all this week anywhere that’s about more than 3 or 4ft above sea level,” Swain said on Monday. “There is essentially no risk for the majority of the land area.
“Folks even miles away from the water and hundreds of feet above sea level were advised that significant flooding was possible,” Swain said. “I just want to repeat: that does not appear to be in the cards.”
But concerns over more targeted impacts from the high water levels remain. As Thanksgiving week brings some of the year’s busiest travel days, experts have been pointing to flooding risks at the low-lying San Francisco international airport, and Oakland San Francisco Bay airport, both major travel hubs. United Airlines is offering free changes to passengers who have flights to, from or through SFO on Wednesday, when the king tides are scheduled to peak, the San Francisco Chronicle reported.
Waymo, a self-driving car service, agreed to suspend its activity in San Francisco starting on Monday, after Waymo vehicles stalled in heavy waters and passengers reported dramatic delays during heavy rainstorms last week, ABC7 News reported.
In Orange county, in Southern California, a meteorologist warned that king tide flooding this week could be worse than the 27 October coastal flooding that damaged 114 structures in Huntington Beach and left others in southern California commuting via kayak, the Los Angeles Times reported.
“It’ll most likely be at least as bad as that, and it could be a little worse because we are actually expecting a little bit of higher surf,” meteorologist Philip Gonsalves told the Los Angeles Times.
digest_he:
רשויות החירום והתחבורה בקליפורניה נערכות להצפות חופיות חמורות עקב תופעת גאות קיצונית, הידועה כגאות מלך, המתרחשת במקביל לתנאי מזג אוויר סוערים המושפעים מתופעת אל ניניו. אזור מפרץ סן פרנסיסקו מסתמן כמוקד הסיכון המרכזי לשיבושים בתנועה ובנמלי התעופה המקומיים, כאשר חברת התעופה יונייטד איירליינס וכלי רכב אוטונומיים של חברת Waymo נערכים בהתאם ומשהים פעילות באזורים המועדים להצפות.

למרות הערכות מוקדמות שדיברו על סערה חסרת תקדים, מומחי אקלים ומראשי הערים ציינו כי התחזיות עודכנו והסכנה מוגבלת בעיקר לאזורים הנמוכים הסמוכים מידי לקו החוף ולמפרץ. עם זאת, רשויות התחבורה ממליצות לציבור הנוסעים היוצאים לחופשת ההודיה להיערך היטב לעיכובים אפשריים בצירים המרכזיים ובנמלי התעופה המרכזיים סן פרנסיסקו ואוקלנד.
